title: How Signals End: Clearance Sets Lifetime
endLine: Clearance ends signals and sets lifetime, trading local reach against tempo.

scenes.tts: Blood carries far signals, tiny gaps pass fast ones, and receptors choose who answers. Once a message turns a cell on, what shuts it off? A signal that cannot end is a switch stuck on.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map without resetting: a TEAL blood vessel runs across the bottom, a nerve-to-receiver synaptic gap sits upper left, and a tissue field of GREEN receptor-bearing cells fills centre-right. Keep YELLOW for messenger dots, GREEN for lit targets, GOLD for time bars and curves, and RED for stop or warning cues. Add CORAL for clearing enzymes, BLUE for reuptake transporters, and PURPLE for sticky matrix fibers. Keep 'schematic' at lower right. YELLOW dots cross the gap and ride the TEAL vessel, lighting GREEN receptor cups. Hold YELLOW dots inside one GREEN cup while a RED warning glow pulses on a stuck toggle labelled 'switch stuck on', and a large question mark rises above the gap.
scenes.narration: Blood carries far signals, tiny gaps pass fast ones, and receptors choose who answers. Once a message turns a cell on, what shuts it off? A signal that cannot end is a switch stuck on.

scenes.visual: Over the carried tissue-and-vessel world, show the title 'How Signals End: Clearance Sets Lifetime' for two seconds. YELLOW messenger dots drift gently beside lit GREEN receptor cups while the TEAL vessel flows steadily along the bottom.

scenes.tts: One way cells end signals is by clearing the messenger. Enzymes can destroy it outside. Transporters can pump it back into the sender or nearby glia. Blood flow or diffusion out of a tiny gap also sweeps it away.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the extracellular space between a sending cell on the left and a GREEN receiver on the right while YELLOW messenger dots drift across. Show three clearing routes in turn without resetting the scene: a CORAL enzyme block cuts YELLOW dots into fading fragments labelled 'enzyme destroys'; a BLUE pump channel on the sending membrane pulls YELLOW dots back inside labelled 'transporter pumps back'; and sweeping arrows carry dots out toward the TEAL vessel below labelled 'flow or diffusion'. Bring up a GOLD gauge beside one YELLOW dot labelled 'lifetime (τ)'. Keep at most 6 items on screen.
scenes.narration: One way cells end signals is by clearing the messenger. Enzymes can destroy it outside. Transporters can pump it back into the sender or nearby glia. Blood flow or diffusion out of a tiny gap also sweeps it away.

scenes.tts: Each route sets lifetime, called tau: the average time one molecule survives. A signal that loses the same fraction each second has no sharp edge. How fast a molecule wanders is its diffusion coefficient, D. Reach, where the signal falls to about a third, is near the square root of D times tau.
scenes.caption: Each route sets lifetime, called τ: the average time one molecule survives. A signal that loses the same fraction each second has no sharp edge. How fast a molecule wanders is its diffusion coefficient, D. Reach, where the signal falls to about a third, is near √(D × τ).
scenes.visual: Hold on the paracrine tissue field: the sending cell at left emits a steady stream of YELLOW dots into uniform space as CORAL clearing sites fade them at a steady fractional rate. Above the tissue, draw a smooth GOLD concentration curve computed as e^(-x/λ) from the source, fading smoothly with no sharp wall. Place a GOLD bracket from the source to where the curve drops to about a third of its source height, labelled 'reach ≈ √(D × τ)', while the GOLD 'lifetime τ' bar stays visible at upper right. No molecular structure appears.
scenes.narration: Each route sets lifetime, called τ: the average time one molecule survives. A signal that loses the same fraction each second has no sharp edge. How fast a molecule wanders is its diffusion coefficient, D. Reach, where the signal falls to about a third, is near √(D × τ).

scenes.tts: Here is the guiding tradeoff. Clearance sets a messenger's lifetime, and lifetime buys reach at the cost of tempo. When release stops, concentration falls on that lifetime scale. Longer life reaches farther, yet takes longer to clear.
scenes.visual: Keep the same sender, YELLOW cloud, GOLD decay curve, and GOLD 'lifetime τ' bar. First speed up clearance: the GOLD bar shrinks, the YELLOW cloud contracts close to the sender, and when release halts the cloud and curve drop briskly under the label 'short life: quick clear'. Then slow clearance: the GOLD bar stretches, the YELLOW cloud spreads wider across more GREEN cells, and when release halts the curve sinks sluggishly while a GOLD clock sweeps slowly under 'long life: slow clear'.
scenes.narration: Here is the guiding tradeoff. Clearance sets a messenger's lifetime, and lifetime buys reach at the cost of tempo. When release stops, concentration falls on that lifetime scale. Longer life reaches farther, yet takes longer to clear.

scenes.tts: Test that bargain in water. A secreted protein lasting four seconds fades over about twenty micrometers, one or two cells. Now slow clearance twenty-five times, to one hundred seconds. Does it reach twenty-five times farther, or much less?
scenes.caption: Test that bargain in water. A secreted protein lasting 4 seconds fades over about 20 µm, one or two cells. Now slow clearance 25 times, to 100 seconds. Does it reach 25 times farther, or much less?
scenes.visual: Keep the sender at left on a calibrated distance axis computed for D = 10^-6 cm²/s, labelled 'water upper bound'. Show the initial YELLOW cloud spanning one or two GREEN cells with a GOLD bracket labelled 'τ = 4 s → 20 µm'. Stretch the GOLD lifetime bar 25-fold to 'τ = 100 s'. Extend two dashed candidate arrows from the sender: a long arrow reaching toward '500 µm?' and a shorter arrow labelled 'much less?'. Display across the top: '25× lifetime: 25× reach, or less?'
scenes.narration: Test that bargain in water. A secreted protein lasting 4 seconds fades over about 20 µm, one or two cells. Now slow clearance 25 times, to 100 seconds. Does it reach 25 times farther, or much less?

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep the top question '25× lifetime: 25× reach, or less?' and both dashed candidate arrows visible. YELLOW dots drift gently inside the 20 µm zone and the stretched GOLD 'τ = 100 s' bar pulses softly. Do not extend the cloud or highlight an answer.

scenes.tts: Much less. Reach grows as the square root of lifetime, and the square root of twenty-five is five. So the reach grows only five times, from twenty to about one hundred micrometers, or five to ten cells. Meanwhile decay slows twenty-five times.
scenes.caption: Much less. Reach grows as the square root of lifetime, and √25 = 5. So the reach grows only 5 times, from 20 to about 100 µm, or five to ten cells. Meanwhile decay slows 25 times.
scenes.visual: Cross out '500 µm?' in RED and light the computed 100 µm mark in GOLD (from √(10^-6 × 100) cm = 100 µm). The YELLOW cloud expands smoothly across five to ten GREEN cells, bracketed '5× reach (100 µm)'. In an inset computed plot of reach against lifetime, draw the square-root curve through (4 s, 20 µm) and (100 s, 100 µm). When release stops, a GOLD clock sweeps 25 turns as the cloud slowly fades, labelled '25× slower decay'.
scenes.narration: Much less. Reach grows as the square root of lifetime, and √25 = 5. So the reach grows only 5 times, from 20 to about 100 µm, or five to ten cells. Meanwhile decay slows 25 times.

scenes.tts: Real tissue is not water. Matrix fibers and receptors bind a drifting protein, slowing its spread. At equal lifetime, a thousandfold lower diffusion coefficient shrinks reach about thirtyfold. The square root of a thousand is about thirty-two. Binding can also protect the molecule and lengthen its life. Either way, a signal to neighbors stays local.
scenes.visual: Keep the same paracrine tissue field at τ = 100 s, then weave PURPLE matrix fibers and GREEN surface cups through the space between cells. YELLOW dots briefly stick to PURPLE fibers and release slowly, winding instead of gliding. On the computed distance axis, shrink the GOLD reach bracket roughly thirtyfold from '100 µm (water)' to 'about 3 µm (sticky tissue)', matching D = 10^-9 cm²/s at 100 s. Show a faint shield outline around one bound dot labelled 'binding may protect'.
scenes.narration: Real tissue is not water. Matrix fibers and receptors bind a drifting protein, slowing its spread. At equal lifetime, a thousandfold lower diffusion coefficient shrinks reach about thirtyfold. √1000 ≈ 32. Binding can also protect the molecule and lengthen its life. Either way, a signal to neighbors stays local.
scenes.caption: Real tissue is not water. Matrix fibers and receptors bind a drifting protein, slowing its spread. At equal lifetime, a thousandfold lower diffusion coefficient shrinks reach about thirtyfold. √1000 ≈ 32. Binding can also protect the molecule and lengthen its life. Either way, a signal to neighbors stays local.

scenes.tts: The synapse takes this tradeoff to an extreme. There an enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, destroys the transmitter acetylcholine within about a millisecond. The same square-root rule gives only a rough scale, near one micrometer. Wiping the gap clean keeps rapid impulses distinct. Other synapses clear serotonin by pumping it back.
scenes.caption: The synapse takes this tradeoff to an extreme. There an enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, destroys the transmitter acetylcholine within about 1 millisecond. The same square-root rule gives only a rough scale, near 1 µm. Wiping the gap clean keeps rapid impulses distinct. Other synapses clear serotonin by pumping it back.
scenes.visual: Pan smoothly to the narrow synaptic gap at upper left of the carried world. Three rapid bursts of YELLOW dots cross the gap to GREEN cups. CORAL acetylcholinesterase blocks inside the gap snip each burst away in a flash, letting the GREEN receiver blink on and cleanly off between impulses; show a GOLD badge 'about 1 ms' and a faint dashed halo labelled '≈ 1 µm rough scale'. Then transform the clearing tool into a BLUE transporter on the sending membrane pulling YELLOW dots back in, labelled 'serotonin reuptake'. Keep 'schematic' at lower right.
scenes.narration: The synapse takes this tradeoff to an extreme. There an enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, destroys the transmitter acetylcholine within about 1 millisecond. The same square-root rule gives only a rough scale, near 1 µm. Wiping the gap clean keeps rapid impulses distinct. Other synapses clear serotonin by pumping it back.

scenes.tts: Circulation, not diffusion, sets a hormone's range. Still, clearance helps set how fast it fades once secretion stops. Epinephrine falls by half in roughly two to three minutes, fading unless the gland keeps sending.
scenes.caption: Circulation, not diffusion, sets a hormone's range. Still, clearance helps set how fast it fades once secretion stops. Epinephrine falls by half in roughly 2 to 3 minutes, fading unless the gland keeps sending.
scenes.visual: Pan down to the first film's TEAL blood vessel running past distant GREEN target cells. YELLOW hormone dots sweep rapidly along the TEAL current under the label 'flow sets range'. Stop release from the gland at left. A computed GOLD decay curve (exponential half-life of 2.5 min, dropping to under a tenth by 10 min) traces downward above the vessel, labelled 'epinephrine: half in 2–3 min'. The YELLOW dots thin out and the GREEN cups dim unless new dots enter the vessel.
scenes.narration: Circulation, not diffusion, sets a hormone's range. Still, clearance helps set how fast it fades once secretion stops. Epinephrine falls by half in roughly 2 to 3 minutes, fading unless the gland keeps sending.

scenes.tts: Ending a message shapes the message itself. Fast removal keeps local signals brief and contained, while lingering buys range only by slowing recovery. What happens when a drug blocks the enzyme or transporter?
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full carried world showing the synaptic gap above, the paracrine tissue field in the middle, and the TEAL vessel below. Highlight the CORAL enzyme in the gap and the BLUE transporter on the sending membrane, then slide a RED question-mark block partway toward each without docking or revealing an outcome, leaving the text's enzyme-block prediction and transporter examples unanswered. Keep 'schematic' at lower right.
scenes.narration: Ending a message shapes the message itself. Fast removal keeps local signals brief and contained, while lingering buys range only by slowing recovery. What happens when a drug blocks the enzyme or transporter?

scenes.visual: End card with one line only: 'Clearance ends signals and sets lifetime, trading local reach against tempo.' Set it large and centred on the dark background. No title, logo, URL, subtitle or smaller line appears. Behind it at low contrast, YELLOW dots fade gently from left to right beside a slowly pulsing GOLD lifetime bar.
